newsitem.title: ITALY: Hard-left stands firm in Italian budget battle.
newsitem.headline: Hard-left stands firm in Italian budget battle.

text.p: The hard left Communist Refoundation party, whose support will be vital to passage of Italy's 1997 budget, reaffirmed on Wednesday that it would not countenance cuts in pensions and health spending.

Party leader Fausto Bertinotti said after talks with Prime Minister Romano Prodi that he had "repeated our positions" on spending and declined to say whether he expected an agreement on the budget to emerge.
A spokesman for Prodi said separately that the prime minister saw no risk of his centre-left government falling over the budget issue.
Prodi's government depends on Communist Refoundation for a majority in the lower house of parliament.
It is now putting the finishing touches to a 1997 budget which Prodi hopes will cut next year's deficit by at least 32.4 trillion lire ($21 billion).
Many economic commentators expect the government to raise the target in the face of worsening 1996 accounts.

A summit of leaders of parties in the government and Bertinotti to discuss the budget had been due to take place on Wednesday but was put back 24 hours to give Prodi more time for talks with ministers.
The government is portraying the budget as crucial to Italy's chances of meeting the strict economic criteria to join a planned single European currency from the start in 1999.

The Treasury Ministry is pushing for cuts to sensitive areas of welfare spending and is also considering introducing a special "solidarity tax" to help boost finances and pull Italy closer to meeting the conditions. $1 = 1,511 lire
